questions.text: Let $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ be a quadratic polynomial such that f(-2) $+f(3)=0$. If one of the roots of $f(x)=0$ is -1 , then the sum of the roots of $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=0$ is equal to :

options.D:
$\frac{14}{3}$

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)

Sol. $f(-2)+f(3)=0$
$$\begin{array}{l}
f(x)=(x+1)(a x+b) \\
f(-2)+f(3)=-1(-2 a+b)+4(3 a+b)=0 \\
2 a-b+12 a+4 b=0 \\
14 a+3 b=0 \\
\frac{-b}{a}=\frac{14}{3}
\end{array}$$

Sum of roots $=\left(-1+\frac{-\mathrm{b}}{\mathrm{a}}\right)=-1+\frac{14}{3}=\frac{11}{3}$
